- Long operating history - FY 2025-26 is the Company's 88th Annual Report
- Presence across both stainless/alloy long steel products and industrial machinery, with the machinery and gear box business housed in wholly owned subsidiary Mukand Heavy Engineering Limited

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Air quality and emissions compliance — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: air emissions from iron and steel production present significant compliance and reputational risks, driven by increasing public health concerns and stricter environmental regulation enforced by authorities such as the Central Pollution Control Board. Mitigation is through advanced air pollution control equipment such as electrostatic precipitators and scrubbers, real-time emissions monitoring, regular internal audits and compliance with applicable air quality norms.
- Hazardous waste management — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: steelmaking generates significant volumes of hazardous waste including slag, dust and sludge, with streams such as Electric Arc Furnace dust posing environmental and health risks from toxic constituents. Rising regulatory scrutiny raises compliance and operating costs, and improper disposal or legacy waste can create long-term liabilities including environmental remediation and site restoration.
- GHG emissions and carbon intensity — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: iron and steel manufacturing is inherently carbon-intensive, and the sector continues to lag others in carbon efficiency despite improvements in emission intensity per tonne. Production also releases SOx, NO2, CO, lead, manganese, particulate matter, hazardous air pollutants and VOCs, keeping air pollution a critical issue under heightened regulatory oversight.
- Energy intensity and Scope 2 exposure — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: steel manufacturing relies heavily on direct fossil fuel combustion and grid electricity, with grid supply contributing significantly to indirect Scope 2 emissions. The choice of production technology (Electric Arc Furnace versus integrated Basic Oxygen Furnace) and fuel type determines the balance between fossil fuel use and electricity dependency.
- Input cost and energy price volatility from geopolitics — The MD&A notes that heightened tensions in parts of the Middle East and continued disruption to key maritime trade routes drove volatility in energy and freight markets; for a sector dependent on global raw material and logistics networks this produced fluctuations in input and energy costs, affecting procurement planning and operating margins.
- Trade remedy measures, safeguards and tariffs — The MD&A notes the industry remained influenced during 2025-26 by increasing use of trade remedy measures, safeguard actions and tariff interventions by several economies to protect domestic steel industries amid persistent global overcapacity and trade diversion; steel trade flows remain influenced by evolving global market conditions, trade policies and pricing dynamics.
- Subdued global demand and China moderation — The MD&A describes a challenging macroeconomic environment with subdued global demand growth, apparent steel demand broadly flat at approximately 1.75 billion tonnes, and China's consumption on a moderating trajectory due to real estate weakness and slower industrial activity, with demand across some major economies largely flat.
- Rising employee and worker turnover — The BRSR turnover-rate disclosure shows the permanent workers turnover rate at 5.46% in FY 2025-26 against 3.37% in FY 2024-25 and 2.90% in FY 2023-24, an upward trend over the three years disclosed.

business.body: Mukand Limited (CIN L99999MH1937PLC002726, registered office at Bajaj Bhawan, Nariman Point, Mumbai) is a manufacturing company whose main business activity is described in its BRSR as 'Steel and heavy machinery'. Its products accounting for 90% of turnover are alloy steel billets and blooms; stainless steel billets, blooms, bars and rods; and EOT cranes, material handling equipment, other industrial machinery and comprehensive engineering services. The Company operates through a Steel Division and an Industrial Machinery Division, serves customers exclusively in the B2B sector, and states that its stainless steel products are essential across engineering, power generation, construction and several other specialised sectors.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Steel Division:** Alloy Steel Billets and Blooms, Stainless Steel Billets and Blooms, Stainless Steel Bars and Rods
- **Industrial Machinery Division:** EOT Cranes, Material Handling Equipment, Other Industrial Machinery, Comprehensive Engineering services
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Mukand Sumi Metal Processing Limited (MSMPL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding). Engaged in manufacturing, trading, purchase, refinement, preparation, import, export and sale of iron and steel in all forms and by-products, and in stainless steel cold finished bars and wires and treasury and investment business. Also a related party for sales/purchase of goods and rendering/receiving of services on an arm's length basis with a 7-day credit period.
- Mukand Heavy Engineering Limited (MHEL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding), incorporated to carry on business in Industrial Machinery and Gear Box Manufacturing; transferee of the Company's machine building business under the slump sale. Also a related party for rendering/receiving of services on an arm's length basis with a 7-day credit period.
- Mukand Sumi Special Steel Limited (MSSSL) — JV: Joint venture with Sumitomo Corporation, Japan, in the business of manufacturing and marketing alloy steel bars and rods. Also a related party for sales/purchase of goods and rendering/receiving of services on an arm's length basis with a 7-day credit period.
- Hospet Steels Limited (HSL) — JV: Joint venture; extent of holding 39.00%; significant influence arises from the extent of shareholding. Listed in the BRSR holding/subsidiary/associate/JV table as a joint venture.
- Bombay Forgings Limited (BFL) — associate: Associate company; 33.17% of shares held by the entity; significant influence arises from the extent of shareholding.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- The Company's stated intent for FY 2025-26 is to distribute to both classes of shareholders while retaining access to debt funding. The AGM notice puts to members a dividend on the 8% Cumulative Redeemable Preference Shares at 8% of paid-up value and an equity dividend of Rs. 3 per share, which explicitly includes a special payout of Re. 1 per share marking 100 years of the Bajaj Group. Members are separately asked to renew, in supersession of the resolution passed at the 87th AGM, a general approval for the Board to issue secured or unsecured redeemable non-convertible debentures in one or more series or tranches aggregating up to Rs. 500 crore on a private placement basis. The Company has had no pecuniary relations or transactions with its non-executive and independent directors other than sitting fees, fees for professional services and reimbursement of expenses, and confirms that no related-party contract or arrangement during FY 2025-26 was other than at arm's length.
- Air emissions control programme: investment in advanced air pollution control equipment such as electrostatic precipitators and scrubbers, implementation of real-time emissions monitoring systems, regular internal audits, and full compliance with applicable air quality norms.
- Hazardous waste programme: waste minimisation by optimising production processes, reuse and recycling of by-products within operations, deployment of advanced treatment technologies and proactive pollution prevention, and continued investment in cleaner technologies and process innovation.
- All waste management activities conducted in strict adherence to the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016.
- The Company has formally identified material environmental and social issues presenting risks or opportunities to the business, with rationale, mitigation approach and financial implications, and states there was no negative financial impact from these material issues in the reporting year 2025-26.
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone and covers the plants at Kalwe, Dighe, Thane District (Maharashtra) and Hospet, Ginigera, Koppal District (Karnataka); the assurance provider and type of assurance obtained are both stated as Not Applicable, i.e. no external assurance on the BRSR.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place across stakeholder groups: designated Plant Head and Plant HR contacts for community grievances, a statutory mechanism for investors, a published shareholder grievance policy, a Whistle Blower Policy for employees and workers, and a POSH Policy with an Internal Complaints Committee for sexual harassment complaints.
- Women's representation on the Board of Directors disclosed at 16.67%.
- CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and CSR activities are carried out by the Company, its joint venture companies and by the Bajaj Group; the CSR Committee comprises Shri Niraj Bajaj (Chairman), Shri R Sankaran and Shri Nirav Bajaj.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no greenfield capex project, capacity addition or commissioning timeline. Change in the Company's footprint during FY 2025-26 came instead from portfolio restructuring. The NCLT, Mumbai Bench, by order dated April 29, 2025, sanctioned the Scheme of Demerger of the Stainless Steel Cold Finished Bars and Wires Undertaking of wholly owned subsidiary Mukand Sumi Metal Processing Limited into Mukand Limited on a going-concern basis; the scheme became effective on May 12, 2025 from the appointed date of April 01, 2024, bringing that undertaking into the parent. In the opposite direction, under a Business Transfer Agreement dated October 18, 2025, the Company transferred part of its Industrial Machinery business - designing, manufacturing, erecting and commissioning EOT cranes, other materials handling and process plant equipment - to its wholly owned subsidiary Mukand Heavy Engineering Limited by way of a slump sale on a going-concern basis, completed on March 31, 2026, with consideration discharged in equity shares of the transferee. The Company also states that there have been no material changes and commitments affecting its financial position between the end of the financial year and the date of the Board's Report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian steel demand supported by large-scale public and private investment in infrastructure - highways, railways, ports, airports, urban infrastructure and renewable energy projects.
- Automotive, capital goods, engineering, construction and manufacturing sectors contributing significantly to incremental domestic steel consumption.
- Divergent regional demand: China's consumption moderating on real-estate weakness and slower industrial activity, while India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East record relatively stronger growth.
- Domestic consumption described as resilient at nearly 164 million tonnes, growing approximately 7.6% over the previous year.
- Indian finished steel exports up nearly 36% to approximately 6.6 million tonnes, supported by competitive pricing, improved product offerings and stronger demand in the Middle East, Europe and Southeast Asia.
- Input-cost and margin pressure from geopolitical tension and disruption to maritime trade routes, causing volatility in energy and freight markets and affecting procurement planning and operating margins.
- Increasing use of trade remedy measures, safeguard actions and tariff interventions by several economies amid persistent global overcapacity and trade diversion.
- Structural decarbonisation shift in the global steel industry - investment in Electric Arc Furnace technology, higher adoption of scrap-based manufacturing, energy efficiency improvements and early-stage hydrogen-based steelmaking.

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.
